errors.quote: A triple $T$ has indicator $t_T$ with $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S∩T|-1$ ... and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$. So each line $\langle t_T\rangle$ is nondegenerate, and neighbors' lines are orthogonal.
errors.problem: These values hold only for the rational form x^T(I-J/9)y, yet the page states them right after defining both the bit and the phase form, with no restriction. For the phase form on F_2^h they are false: the paper has t_T.t_T=1 (2 would be 0, making every line degenerate). Also t_S.t_T=|S∩T| mod 2, so the complex neighbors (distinct triples with even intersection) are orthogonal, whereas |S∩T|-1 would be odd for them. The complex case's nondegeneracy and orthogonality are therefore derived from a wrong formula.

errors.quote: A nonzero residual contains a coordinate unit vector, hence an orthonormal basis
errors.problem: Residuals with a factor P or Q (e.g. P⊗F⊗Q, B⊗F⊗Q) contain no coordinate unit vector of F^{⊗3}. The paper instead builds a norm-one vector by tensoring coordinate units in the factors with the norm-one vectors of P and Q. It then uses nondegeneracy of the residual, the fact that a binary space is nonalternating iff it has a norm-one vector, and the fact that a nondegenerate nonalternating space has an orthonormal basis.

errors.quote: let $H$ be the Hadamard matrix, $\operatorname{wt}$ the Hamming weight, $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=aI+bX$
errors.problem: With the usual unnormalized Hadamard matrix [[1,1],[1,-1]], H diag(1,i)H=2(aI+bX) and H diag(1,-1)H=2X. The paper uses H=(1/sqrt2)[[1,1],[1,-1]].

errors.quote: Outgoing labels $A\otimes F$ on $X$ and $B'$ on $Y$ equal the next incoming ones
errors.problem: The page suppresses the factor Q, and it never states the incoming labels. In the paper the outgoing labels are (A⊗F)⊗Q and B'⊗Q, and they equal the next incoming A'⊗<t_{a_{j+1}}>⊗Q' and B'⊗<t_{a_{j+1}}>⊗Q' only after writing Q=<t_{a_{j+1}}>⊗Q'. As written, A⊗F (in F^{⊗j}) is not the next incoming label (in F^{⊗(j+1)}).
m=h^3 is the dimension of the ambient label space F^{⊗3}, not of a label. Labels range in dimension from 0 to m.
